subject: SLAV
title: Language & Minorities in Europe
info: Same as EURO 418, FR 418, GER 418, ITAL 418, LING 418, PS 418, and SPAN 418. See FR 418.

sections.sectionText: Language & Minorities in Europe. Credit: 3 or 4 hours. Survey of regional and immigrant minority language use, policies, and planning across Europe. Focus on political and social issues, such as language regimes, education, loss, and maintenance. Two immigrant languages, Turkish and Arabic/Berber, and four indigenous language families: Balto-Slavic with Estonian, Celtic, Romance with Basque, and Slavic with Hungarian. Taught in English. Same as GER 418, ITAL 418, LING 418, PS 418, SLAV 418, SPAN 418, and EURO 418. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours.

subject: SLAV
title: Slavic Cultural Studies
info: Same as CWL 453. 3 undergraduate hours. 4 graduate hours. May be repeated to a maximum of 6 undergraduate hours or 8 graduate hours in same term; or 9 undergraduate hours or 12 graduate hours in separate terms. Prerequisite: Two years of literature, preferably Russian or East European; or consent of instructor.

sections.sectionText: This course examines historical and scholarly debates about the (post)coloniality of the Central and East European regions. Students will read and analyze new theoretical and empirical studies about the applicability of the colonial and postcolonial paradigms to the region’s past and present.
